body.x: MOVIC Lab Inc. (CEO Lee Wonkeun) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

MOVIC Lab specializes in smart factory solutions based on AI technology. Its flagship service is an AI-based facility fault detection solution that excels in time-series data analysis for various industrial signals, including current, voltage, vibration, temperature, and humidity, combined with high-performance deep learning algorithms.

The company emphasized the importance of early fault detection in manufacturing, stating, "Manufacturing relies heavily on equipment, and failures lead to significant economic losses. Detecting early signs of failure and performing predictive maintenance before breakdowns occur is crucial. However, conventional methods have limitations." MOVIC Lab aims to overcome these limitations by leveraging ultrasonic and AI technologies to improve manufacturing environments and set a new standard for facility management.

The 'WatchBAT' solution, presented at CES 2025, predicts machine failures using ultrasonic data and AI. Ultrasonic data refers to sounds emitted by machines in the ultrasonic frequency range (above 20 kHz), which humans cannot hear. These signals occur before visible signs like vibration, heat, or noise, enabling the detection of subtle changes in manufacturing equipment.

The company explained that ultrasonic sensors are non-contact, making them more versatile than traditional contact sensors. They also quantify equipment conditions, allowing easy and intuitive assessment on-site.

body.cap: Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter, interviews Lee Wonkeun, CEO of MOVIC Lab | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Regarding their participation in CES, a MOVIC Lab representative said, "In Korea, MOVIC Lab is the only company utilizing ultrasonic and AI technology to predict equipment failures, and we've confirmed strong interest from major clients. This being our first CES, we aim to showcase our products (WatchBAT and WatchBAT KIT) and technological expertise in the U.S., a leader in advanced technology, while gauging market responses. Conducting market research for U.S. entry was another reason for our participation. In October, we secured a U.S. patent and plan to identify collaborators and partners to prepare for entry into the U.S. market."

MOVIC Lab targets manufacturers and equipment makers in high-tech industries such as semiconductors, secondary batteries, and displays. Its focus includes local U.S. companies and Korean corporations operating in the U.S. During CES, the company demonstrated its ultrasonic diagnostic solution, explaining the principles of ultrasonic generation and showcasing the differences between audible and ultrasonic sounds.

The representative added, "We are finalizing PoC verification with major Korean companies on mass production lines, and visible revenue is expected next year. We are expanding the range of verified equipment, including pumps, blades, motors, bearings, and actuators. Based on proven domestic references, we plan to collaborate with local companies to enter overseas markets. The U.S., with its well-established cloud infrastructure, is a key market for us. After verifying our solutions on key equipment in the U.S., we aim to offer them as cloud-based SaaS. Additionally, we are working on simplifying our solution to operate via connected ultrasonic sensors on tablets."

Ultrasonic technology extends beyond manufacturing equipment to electrical fault detection and fire prevention applications. Recognizing its vast potential, MOVIC Lab plans to enhance its technology further and expand into safety and fire detection markets.
